title: Why a triangle's angles make 180°
caption: The line through A parallel to BC makes alternate angles equal to B and C. Those two angles and the angle at A fill a straight line, so A + B + C = 180°.
alt: A triangle ABC with a line through A parallel to BC; the angles on the line either side of A equal B and C, and the three angles at A make a straight line.
description: Draw a line through A parallel to BC.
The angle between the line and AB, on the left, equals angle B (alternate angles); the angle between AC and the line, on the right, equals angle C.
The three angles at A lie along a straight line, so together they are 180°: A + B + C = 180°.
